newsitem.title: BELARUS: Chernomyrdin heads for crucial talks in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin heads for crucial talks in Belarus.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin headed for Belarus on Thursday to try to mediate in the country's political conflict three days ahead of a controversial referendum.

Chernomyrdin was expected in the Belarussian capital for a crucial round of talks with hardline President Alexander Lukashenko, who has so far resisted international pressure to drop the referendum and compromise with his opponents.
The Russian premier was accompanied by leaders of Moscow's two houses of parliament, who appear to have reached a consensus with the Kremlin that Lukashenko should be pushed to compromise.
Belarussian officials said talks were expected to begin around 9 p.m. (1900 GMT).
Earlier Itar-Tass news agency reported that Chernomyrdin had already arrived in the Belarussian capital with Russian parliamentary leaders but this appeared to be premature.

Belarussin parliament chairman Semyon Sharetsky said Chernomyrdin would initially hold separate talks with President Alexander Lukashenko while Russian speakers Yegor Stroyev and Gennady Seleznyov would go to parliament.
"Chernomyrdin will go to Lukashenko's residence and Seleznyov and Stroyev will come to parliament," Sharetsky told deputies. "Later there will possibly be a joint meeting."
Mikhail Podgainy, head of Lukashenko's information department, said Lukashenko would meet Chernomyrdin at the airport.

On Wednesday the Belarussian leader snubbed the Russian mediation effort, refusing to go to Smolensk for peace talks with Sharetsky. Voting has already begun in the referendum which his critics say will turn the country into a dictatorship.
Seleznyov told reporters in the Russian capital earlier that Moscow wanted Lukashenko to agree that the referendum on extending his powers should only be advisory, rather than binding.
The future of the Belarussian constitution should be passed to a special constitutional committee, he said.
He said Lukashenko's parliamentary opponents would accept such a deal and were ready to drop their plans to impeach the president.
